answer: Northwind retired two forms in 2026, both on February 1, 2026. NW-ODO-1 (Odometer statement) was replaced by NW-ODO-2 (Odometer disclosure statement). NW-POA-1 (Power of attorney, notarized) was replaced by NW-POA-2 (Power of attorney, e-sign). An NW-POA-1 signed before February 1, 2026 was accepted only until June 30, 2026, so that grace period is over as of today. NW-POA-2 can be signed electronically with no notary, except in Georgia, where it must still be notarized. Also note that the help-center article "Broken or replaced odometer" still tells customers to use NW-ODO-1, so it looks out of date and should point to NW-ODO-2.
